Prior treatment required: Rituximab or equivalent and anthracycline chemotherapy. Prior treatment excluded: Prior CAR-T therapy, systemic gene modifying therapy for B-cell lymphoma, prior allogeneic stem cell transplant, prior BITE antibodies for cancer therapy, or prior T cell receptor-engineered T cell therapy. general_exclusion_criteria:
Poor performance status (eg ECOG >1, or ECOG 2 if not due to lymphoma)
Renal dysfunction (creatinine clearance <= 45mL/min)
Cardiac dysfunction (ejection fraction < 45%)
Low resting O2 saturation (<= 90% on room air)
Liver dysfunction (ALT or AST >= 5 times Upper Limit of Normal, or total bilirubin >= 1.5 mg/dl except in individuals with Gilbert's syndrome)
Severe cytopenia (absolute neutrophil count <= 1000/uL, absolute lymphocyte count <= 100/uL, or platelet count <= 50,000/uL)
Short life expectancy (<= 3 months other than primary disease)
HIV infection or active hepatitis B (HBsAg positive)
Hepatitis C virus infection with detectable viral load per quantitative PCR and/or nucleic acid testing
Pharmacologically uncontrolled seizures
Autoimmune CNS disease (eg multiple sclerosis, optic neuritis) or other immunologic or inflammatory disease
For CNS cohort: Midline shift on MRI, abnormal high CSF opening pressure, or CSF protein > 150 mg/dL
Recent whole brain radiotherapy (within 3 months) for CNS cohort
Active systemic fungal, viral, or bacterial infection
Pregnancy or breast-feeding
Previous or concurrent malignancy (except adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma, in situ carcinoma of the cervix or breast treated curatively without recurrence for 2 years, adequately treated breast or prostate carcinoma on hormonal therapies in remission for 2 years, or a primary malignancy completely resected or treated with curative intent and in complete remission for 2 years)
Severely immunocompromised subjects (eg due to current treatment of non-neurologic autoimmune disease)
Medical condition requiring prolonged use of systemic corticosteroids equivalent to prednisone > 10 mg/day
History of myocardial infarction, cardiac angioplasty or stenting, unstable angina, or other clinically significant cardiac disease within 6 months of enrollment
Concurrent radiotherapy
Baseline dementia that would interfere with therapy or monitoring
History of severe immediate hypersensitivity reaction to any of the agents used in the study
Refusal to participate in additional lentiviral gene therapy LTFU protocol

general_exclusion_criteria:
Poor performance status (eg ECOG >1).
Active or progressing brain metastases or evidence of leptomeningeal disease.
Persistent toxicities from previous systemic antineoplastic treatments of Grade >1 (excluding alopecia and vitiligo).
Clinically significant lung disease requiring systemic corticosteroid treatment within the last 6 months (eg interstitial pneumonia, pneumonitis, pulmonary fibrosis, and severe radiation pneumonitis) or suspected such diseases by imaging at screening.
Acute or chronic pancreatitis and/or any cirrhosis except Child-Pugh class A.
Hepatic insufficiency manifesting as clinical jaundice, hepatic encephalopathy, and/or variceal bleed within 60 days prior to study entry.
History of liver transplant.
Prior allogeneic bone marrow transplantation.
Significant cardiac disease including recent myocardial infarction, acute coronary syndromes, congestive heart failure (NYHA class III or IV), uncontrolled hypertension, uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmias, or severe aortic stenosis.
History of thromboembolic or cerebrovascular events including transient ischemic attacks, cerebrovascular accidents, deep vein thrombosis, or pulmonary emboli within 3 months prior to first dose.
Acute and/or clinically significant bacterial, fungal, or viral infection including hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), unless meeting specific stability and treatment criteria.
Pregnancy or breast-feeding.
Prior history of malignancy other than inclusion diagnosis within 3 years prior to first dose (excluding adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer, non-invasive superficial bladder cancer, in situ cervical cancer, in situ breast cancer, or in situ prostate cancer).
Any other severe acute or chronic medical or psychiatric conditions or laboratory abnormality that would make the patient inappropriate for enrollment.

general_exclusion_criteria: Poor performance status (ECOG >= 2). Active brain metastases or known carcinomatous meningitis. History of glaucoma, retinal vein occlusion, retinal pathology, corneal erosion, corneal degeneration, active or recurrent keratitis, or intraocular pressure > 21 mm Hg. History of rhabdomyolysis or neuromuscular disorders associated with elevated creatine kinase. Uncontrolled intercurrent illness including uncontrolled hypertension, unstable angina pectoris, uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia, congestive heart failure (New York Heart Association Class III or IV), active ischemic heart disease, myocardial infarction within the previous six months, syncope of cardiovascular etiology, ventricular arrhythmia of pathological origin, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, severe obstructive pulmonary disease, or severe chronic liver or renal disease. History of a second malignancy (except those deemed low risk for recurrence or specific types like cervical cancer in situ or non-melanoma skin cancer). History of allergic reactions to abemaciclib, fulvestrant, or VS-6766. Known history of HIV with an AIDS-defining opportunistic infection within the past 12 months or requirement for strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers. Known active hepatitis B virus or hepatitis C virus infection (unless stable or cured per protocol). Use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers. Pregnancy or breastfeeding. Inability to swallow oral medications, impaired gastrointestinal absorption, preexisting Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, or preexisting chronic condition resulting in baseline Grade 2 or higher diarrhea. Active systemic bacterial infection requiring intravenous antibiotics, active fungal infection requiring intravenous antifungal treatment, or SARS-CoV-2 infection within 28 days prior to first dose. Treatment with warfarin. Other serious or uncontrolled preexisting medical conditions such as interstitial lung disease or severe dyspnea.

general_exclusion_criteria:
Poor performance status (eg ECOG > 1).
LVEF < 50%.
Inadequate organ functions.
Symptomatic congestive heart failure (New York Heart Association classes II-IV) or serious cardiac arrhythmia requiring treatment.
Myocardial infarction or unstable angina within 6 months before enrollment.
Clinically important abnormalities in rhythm, conduction or morphology of resting electrocardiogram (eg complete left bundle branch block, third-degree heart block, second-degree heart block, or PR interval > 250 milliseconds).
QTcF prolongation > 470 milliseconds.
Unable or unwilling to discontinue concomitant drugs known to prolong the QT interval.
History of non-infectious interstitial lung disease, pneumonitis, and/or radiation pneumonitis that required steroids, current interstitial lung disease, pneumonitis, and/or radiation pneumonitis, or suspected interstitial lung disease, pneumonitis, and/or radiation pneumonitis that cannot be ruled out by imaging.
Lung-specific intercurrent clinically significant illness (eg pulmonary emboli within 3 months, severe asthma, severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disorder, restrictive lung disease, significant pleural effusion) or autoimmune, connective tissue or inflammatory disorder with pulmonary involvement, or prior complete pneumonectomy.
Uncontrolled infection requiring intravenous antibiotics, antivirals, or antifungals.
Clinically significant corneal disease.
Known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection.
Active viral hepatitis (except for HBsAg positive subjects with HBV DNA < 1000 cps/mL or 100 IU/mL not on suppressive therapy, or HCV positive subjects who completed curative treatment with HCV RNA below the lower limit of quantification).
Pregnancy or lactation.
Clinically active brain metastases (untreated and symptomatic, or requiring steroids or anticonvulsants).
Unresolved toxicities from previous anticancer therapy (NCI-CTCAE version 5.0 grade > 1, excluding alopecia and certain chronic Grade 2 toxicities).
Multiple primary malignancies within 3 years before enrollment (except resected non-melanoma skin cancer, curatively treated in-situ disease, other curatively treated solid tumors, or contralateral breast cancer).
Substance abuse or other medical conditions increasing safety risk.
Hypersensitivity to drug substances or inactive ingredients.
